newsitem.title: USA: U.S. expected to join military mission in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expected to join military mission in Zaire.

text.p: The United States was expected to announce on Wednesday an agreement in principle to participate in an international military force to intervene in Zaire's humanitarian crisis, U.S. officials said.

One official said the U.S. role was expected to involve "a few thousand" American troops who would provide logistical support and secure the airport at Goma in eastern Zaire in order to get humanitarian relief suoplies to more than one million refugees said to be at risk.
But the official stressed that many details remained to be firmed up and the initial U.S. announcement would be an agreement in principle to take part, not a final decision.

The officials were uncertain when the relief operation might begin. A U.S. military assessment team was reported to be in Uganda on Wednesday, trying to get to neighbouring Zaire to assess the situation. It was unknown when the team might report to Washington.

The United States has been under mounting pressure to join in a multinational effort, especially from France and Canada, which has agreed to lead a military force. President Bill Clinton discussed Zaire's refugee crisis with other world leaders by telephone on Wednesday and a White House announcement was expected later, officials said.
